The native Python `xml` library is vulnerable to XML External Entity (XXE) attacks.  These attacks can leak confidential data and "XML bombs" can cause denial of service. Do not use this library to parse untrusted input. Instead  the Python documentation recommends using `defusedxml`.

GitHub Actions step uses a mutable tag or branch reference. Tags and branch names can be silently repointed by the action owner, enabling supply-chain attacks — as seen in the trivy-action and kics-github-action compromises. Pin the reference to a full 40-character commit SHA instead, e.g. `uses: actions/checkout@8ade135a41bc03ea155e62e844d188df1ea18608`.

Affected versions of sharp are vulnerable to Divide By Zero / Heap-based Buffer Overflow / Out-of-bounds Read / Out-of-bounds Write. sharp bundles a vulnerable version of the native libheif library, inheriting two critical memory-safety flaws in derived-item (`iden`) and auxiliary-item (`auxl`) handling: a heap buffer overflow in `scale_nearest_neighbor()` where duplicate alpha planes let a 10/12-bit sample be written into an 8-bit plane allocation with an attacker-controlled overflow size and contents (CVE-2026-84383), and a class of out-of-bounds reads and writes across roughly a dozen pixel-plane consumers that assume a `HeifPixelImage` logical geometry matching every channel plane it holds (GHSA-2jg2-4ch7-h545, for which a working code-execution exploit was confirmed). Decoding a crafted AVIF or HEIF image can therefore corrupt the heap and lead to remote code execution. Because sharp selects the libvips loader by sniffing the input bytes, no call site can be shown to be safe: `sharp(untrustedBuffer)` reaches the libheif loader exactly as `sharp("photo.avif")` does, and even a metadata-only `.metadata()` call parses the container. Upgrade to sharp 0.35.4 or later, which bundles libheif 1.23.2; if you rely on a globally-installed libvips, upgrade that libheif to 1.23.2. Blocking the HEIF-family loader with `sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadHeif"] })` is the only workaround that prevents the vulnerable decode path from being reached; running a `node` binary compiled as a Position Independent Executable merely blunts escalation to code execution and does not stop the heap corruption, and the official Node.js builds are not PIE. The heap corruption itself is platform-independent; the advisory documents escalation to remote code execution on glibc-based Linux hosts running a non-PIE `node` binary, so a finding on macOS or musl still represents an exploitable memory-safety bug.

Affected versions of undici are vulnerable to Uncaught Exception / Unchecked Return Value. An undici `WebSocket` or `WebSocketStream` is opened without requesting any subprotocols. If the server (or a man-in-the-middle on a `ws://` connection) answers the opening handshake with an unrequested `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol` header, undici throws an uncaught `TypeError` inside a microtask, crashing the Node.js process (denial of service).

Affected versions of undici are vulnerable to Improper Certificate Validation. undici's `BalancedPool` deep-clones its constructor options with a JSON round-trip before passing them to its upstream pools, so function values in the `connect` or `tls` options (such as a `checkServerIdentity` callback or a custom connector) are silently dropped. Custom TLS certificate verification never runs, and certificates that pass Node's default checks are accepted, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks against applications that rely on certificate pinning or custom identity checks.

Affected versions of sharp are vulnerable to Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component / Use After Free. The prebuilt libvips binaries shipped with sharp bundle a vulnerable librsvg that has a use-after-free when decoding SVG images, which can lead to remote code execution when sharp processes an attacker-supplied SVG. Upgrade to sharp 0.35.5 or later, or block SVG decoding with sharp.block({ operation: ["VipsForeignLoadSvg"] }).
